name: The Fitzwilliam Hotel
positioning: Boutique hotel on St. Stephen's Green at the start of Grafton Street in central Dublin, with Green-view terrace rooms and a Penthouse with its own butler
best_for: Couples who want a central Dublin base on St. Stephen's Green
Travelers who want a room with a private terrace over the Green
Guests celebrating in style in a Penthouse with a private butler

facts.text: The hotel is on St. Stephen's Green at the beginning of Grafton Street, Dublin's main shopping avenue.
Garden guestrooms each overlook the hotel's quiet courtyard.
Deluxe guestrooms have a wool mohair sofa and a free-standing bath.
Deluxe Premium guestrooms offer a choice of a combined bath and shower or a separate Chartreuse bath with a stand-alone shower.
Diptyque toiletries are exclusive to the Deluxe Premium guestrooms.

When guests book a Deluxe Premium guestroom, the hotel matches them with a room suited to their preferences, such as a private terrace overlooking St. Stephen's Green, a four-poster bed or a freestanding bath.
The Penthouse has a baby grand piano.
The Penthouse has rich-fired acacia wood flooring, deep shag pile rugs, a sculpted ceiling and handpicked Italian furnishings.
The lobby is airy and scented with lemongrass, with a bar tucked away at the back.
The hotel is home to Glovers Alley, a restaurant with a pink 1920s dining room and a French-inspired menu.
The hotel can arrange a private car and driver transfer from Dublin Airport.

highlights.text: The Penthouse spans nearly 2,000 square feet at the top of the hotel.
The Penthouse has a private butler available 24/7 who can arrange city tours, reservations or an in-room massage.
Deluxe guestrooms come courtyard-facing or with a private viewing terrace overlooking St. Stephen's Green.
Before a stay, someone from the hotel calls guests to ask what they want from their room.
The Luas tram stops right outside the hotel's front door, reaching Trinity College and the Book of Kells in about two minutes.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the busy city-centre location may not suit guests seeking tranquility.
The hotel draws couples but no large groups, a deliberate decision to keep a boutique feel.
Drivers use the hotel's secure underground car park, accessed from Mercer Street Lower.
